reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes SPS of a different alloy system (W-Ta-Ti-V-Cr) at 1600°C, not the proposed W38Ta36Cr15V11 at 1000°C, and provides no data on grain boundary character, segregation, irradiation response, or hardening. The key premises about defect sink efficiency, precipitation suppression, and hardening retention are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Rapid SPS limits grain growth and prevents excessive grain boundary segregation
Uniform, refined grain boundaries act as efficient defect sinks during irradiation
Reduced heterogeneous nucleation sites suppress radiation-induced Cr/V precipitation
SPS-processed alloy retains negligible irradiation hardening comparable to conventional alloy
SPS parameters (1000°C, 50 MPa, 5 min) produce the required uniform grain boundary network in W38Ta36Cr15V11
